summary: Deferred failover skips pinned cohort during canary quorum delay causing mixed-variant responses
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary for redwood-3b-v1 (customer LexaDocs, dedicated pool) we observed requests from pinned tenant sessions intermittently routed to a degraded fallback variant after the orchestrator delayed quorum confirmation for the canary slice. Impact: Customer reported mixed responses (old variant + degraded variant) for live users; perceptible quality regressions and billing spike due to fallback cost. Environment: prod us-east, dedicated capacity pool 'lexa-dedicated-01', canary rollout with 5% weight and quorum enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start canary promote job for redwood-3b-v1 to 5% weight. 2) Induce short orchestrator leader election (simulate preemptive pod reboot). 3) Observe routing decisions during quorum window while prewarm handshakes are ongoing. 4) Monitor pinned-session routing and fallback triggers. Observed behavior: Orchestrator quorum delay extended the canary cutover window; routing coordinator deferred failover decision and treated pinned sessions as eligible for fallback if they hit edge healthcheck timeouts. Edge produced 502s during leader election which triggered fallback policy; some pinned sessions were not re-affined when orchestrator resumed, resulting in mixed-variant responses. Logs/telemetry: Trace snippets attached in investigation_notes and links to dashboards in related_confluence_pages. Workaround: Temporarily pause canary weight increase and scale up prewarm workers for lexad-dedicated pool; manual pin refresh issued via control-plane API for affected tenant. Next steps: engineering to patch routing coordinator to honor explicit session pins during deferred failover windows and add quorum delay metric alerts.
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2024-11-05: Customer LexaDocs reported mixed outputs and higher per-token costs since 09:12 UTC after canary promotion. Asked for request IDs and tenant IDs. Provided initial grok logs.

Customer (LexaDocs, Aaron Patel) 2024-11-05: Confirmed issue started immediately after we initiated canary. Shared sample request IDs: r_20241105_a1..a5. Noted intermittent degraded completions for pinned users only.
SRE (Priya Rao) 2024-11-05: Reproduced routing entropy correlated with orchestrator leader election at 09:11 UTC. Edge returned 502s for ~18s causing fallback throttle to kick in.

Eng (Liam O'Neill) 2024-11-06: Hypothesis: routing-coordinator's failover decision as implemented treats quorum-delayed slices same as unhealthy. Investigating whether pin handshake is suppressed when prewarm not committed.
Support (Maya Chen) 2024-11-06: Applied immediate mitigation: paused canary weight progression and forced pin-refresh for tenant lexad-123. Customer reports degradation eased at 10:03 UTC.
SRE (Priya Rao) 2024-11-07: Deployed temporary control-plane rule to respect explicit session pins during deferred failover windows in prod-us-east as hotfix; monitoring for regression.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator quorum delay extended canary window and failover logic used 'slice_health' that flagged prewarm-incomplete slices as degraded. Evidence: snapshot of slice_health metrics shows 'PendingQuorum' -> 'Degraded' transition during leader election.

Hypothesis 2: Edge healthcheck 502s during leader election triggered fallback throttle which didn't consult session-pin store. Evidence: edge logs show fallback decisions at 09:11:20 that lack pin-lookup calls.
Test performed: Forced leader election in staging and replayed perf tests; confirmed pinned sessions were eligible for fallback during quorum delay when prewarm ack missing.

Rollforward risk assessment: Patch to routing-coordinator must not disable legitimate fallback for truly unhealthy nodes; propose scoped change to consult explicit pin store before treating a session as eligible for fallback.
resolution: Workaround implemented: paused canary and forced pin-refresh for affected tenants; hotfix deployed to control-plane to honor explicit pins during deferred failover windows in prod-us-east. Follow-ups: engineering to release routing-coordinator patch (PR referenced) with unit and e2e tests, update canary runbook to include quorum-delay detection, add alerting on 'quorum_delay_seconds' > 5s, and schedule postmortem with LexaDocs. Target permanent fix release by 2024-11-12.
